h1: Grand Mandarin Latphrao 130 — Rooms Bigger Than the Price at This Bangkapi Budget Pick
intro: If you want a clean, affordable base in Bangkok's eastern Bangkapi district — steps from local food stalls and a short ride to The Mall Bangkapi — Hotel Grand Mandarin Latphrao 130 is one of those places that quietly punches above its price tag. The 2-star property at 152 Soi Lat Phrao 130 Yaek 2, Khlong Chan has been operating since 2002. What guests consistently highlight most is how surprisingly spacious and spotlessly clean the rooms are for the price. Score: 9.1 out of 92 reviews on Trip.com. Rooms from approximately THB 500/night.

body.html: Hotel Grand Mandarin Latphrao 130 sits at 152 Soi Lat Phrao 130 Yaek 2, Khlong Chan, Bang Kapi — surrounded by local shops and restaurants. The Mall Lifestore Bangkapi is a 3–5 minute drive away, and the Yellow Line MRT Lam Sali station is reachable in around 10–12 minutes by motorcycle taxi or Grab. This combination of nearness to a major mall and budget pricing is its core appeal for travellers with business or shopping plans in the Bangkapi area.

The most frequently mentioned theme across guest reviews is just how generously sized the rooms are relative to the price. For a two-star property, the airy rooms with large beds, private balconies, cable TV, mini-fridge, air-conditioning and en-suite hot-shower bathrooms deliver considerably more than a quick glance at the rate might suggest. Many reviewers use phrases like "super spacious" and "way cleaner than expected" — sentiments that underpin the hotel's strong 9.1 score.
"Room was huge for the price, very clean, fresh white linen, staff were friendly — definitely coming back."

Staff come up repeatedly in positive reviews for being friendly and for remembering returning guests. A 7-Eleven and local food vendors are within walking distance of the entrance, making early breakfasts or late-night snacks easy without spending much. That said, the hotel does not provide a restaurant or breakfast service — this is firmly a bed-only property, and the price reflects that.

The most common gripes from guests are inconsistent Wi-Fi signal strength and a slightly confusing check-in process — the front desk is located in a separate building, and the entrance signage is small enough that some first-timers walk past it. A THB 1,000 cash deposit is collected at check-in, which is standard practice for this type of property in Bangkok but worth knowing ahead of time.

Compared to other Bangkapi options like Metro Point or IMM Hotel, Grand Mandarin Latphrao 130 comes in noticeably cheaper while maintaining strong cleanliness scores. It suits budget-conscious travellers who simply want a spacious, clean room as a base for shopping at The Mall Bangkapi, or for anyone who needs an affordable east-Bangkok foothold without paying for amenities they won't use.

There is no swimming pool, no on-site restaurant and no parking. None of these are surprises at this price point — and for a hotel scoring 9.1 from 92 genuine guest reviews, the core proposition of clean, roomy accommodation at under THB 700 per night clearly lands well with the people who stay here.

honestSummary: Grand Mandarin Latphrao 130 is a budget hotel where the rooms are genuinely bigger and cleaner than the price implies. It is a solid choice for price-conscious travellers with plans in Bangkapi, but come knowing there is no parking, no breakfast and Wi-Fi can be patchy.
honestChecks: If you need on-site parking — the hotel has a strict No Parking policy; street parking or nearby facilities are your only option → plan to arrive by Grab or motorcycle taxi instead
If reliable fast Wi-Fi is critical — guest reviews flag intermittent connectivity issues → bring a local SIM data plan as a backup
If you expect on-site breakfast or a restaurant — none available at the property, though 7-Eleven and local food stalls are immediately outside → not a dealbreaker, just plan ahead

tips.title: Skip Driving — Use Grab
tips.body: The hotel has no parking. Grab or a motorcycle taxi from Yellow Line MRT Lam Sali station takes about 10 minutes and costs roughly THB 40–60.

tips.title: Bring THB 1,000 Cash
tips.body: A THB 1,000 cash deposit is collected at check-in. It is refunded in full at check-out as long as there is no damage to the room.

tips.title: Breakfast is a Short Walk Away
tips.body: A 7-Eleven and local food stalls are right outside the hotel — rice dishes, noodle soups and Thai iced coffees from about THB 30–80 starting early morning.

tips.title: Pack a Local SIM
tips.body: Hotel Wi-Fi works but can drop in signal strength. If you need to stream video or work remotely, a local data SIM (available at Suvarnabhumi, Don Mueang or 7-Eleven) is good insurance.

faqTitle: Hotel Grand Mandarin Latphrao 130 — Frequently Asked Questions

faq.q: Where exactly is Hotel Grand Mandarin Latphrao 130, and what is nearby?
faq.a: The hotel is at 152 Soi Lat Phrao 130 Yaek 2, Khlong Chan, Bang Kapi, Bangkok 10240. The Mall Lifestore Bangkapi is 3–5 minutes away by car. Yellow Line MRT Lam Sali station is approximately 10–12 minutes by motorcycle taxi or Grab.

faq.q: How much does a room cost at Grand Mandarin Latphrao 130?
faq.a: Rooms start from approximately THB 500–800 per night depending on room type and season. The Standard Queen Bed room is the main offering and represents excellent value at this price point.

faq.q: Is there parking at Hotel Grand Mandarin Latphrao 130?
faq.a: No — the hotel explicitly states No Parking. Guests are advised to arrive by Grab, taxi or motorcycle taxi. Street parking may be available nearby but is not guaranteed.
No breakfast service is provided. However, a 7-Eleven convenience store and local food stalls are right outside the hotel where you can buy food from early morning for around THB 30–80.

faq.q: Who is Hotel Grand Mandarin Latphrao 130 best suited for?
faq.a: It is ideal for budget travellers who need a clean, spacious base in Bangkapi — shoppers heading to The Mall, people with business in the area, or anyone wanting affordable accommodation in eastern Bangkok. Less suited for families needing parking, or travellers requiring on-site dining.
